descriptionChirho: An Aramaic noun meaning writing, a written document, or a decree. Found predominantly in Daniel 5-6 (the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast and Darius's written decree) and in Ezra 6:18 and 7:22 (written prescriptions and regulations). All occurrences -- whether emphatic state (כְּתָבָא, the writing), absolute (כְתָב, writing), construct with preposition (כִּכְתָב, as written/prescribed), or with conjunction (וּכְתָבָא, and the writing) -- refer to the same fundamental concept of written text or an official written document. Multilingual glosses are highly consistent: Arabic الكتابة (the writing), German Schrift (writing/scripture), Hindi लेख (writing/article), Korean 글/문서 (writing/document), Spanish escritura/documento (writing/document), French ecrit/ecriture (writing).
